newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen top-heavy in Asia with focus on FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen top-heavy in Asia with focus on FOMC.

text.p: The dollar is expected to remain top-heavy against the yen and stay range-bound on Tuesday as the market will be largely focused on whether the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) will tighten credit at its policy-setting meeting later in the day, dealers said.
"Trade may be dominated by interbank traders ahead of the FOMC meeting," a city bank dealer said, adding that the dollar would stay mostly in the 115-116 yen range.
"It may dip briefly below 115 yen, but I don't think traders will keep buying yen aggressively through that level unless there is a fresh factor to do so," he added.
A trust bank dealer said offers from exporters and some trust banks may emerge above 116 yen, keeping the greenback's topside heavy.
Weakness of the mark against the yen may also weigh on the dollar versus the yen, dealers said.
The mark slid against the British pound and the Italian lira overnight, which indirectly pushed the mark/yen rate below 68 yen.
Dealers said the German currency may remain bearish against the yen during Asian trading time with no substantial bids expected on the downside.
Dealers said trade may stay range-bound as the market awaits the FOMC meeting later in the day to find clues to the future direction of the dollar/yen rate.

The Fed raised rates for the first time in more than two years on March 25, but Wall Street remains divided on whether a second such move is necessary given signs of an economic slowdown in April data.

A Reuters poll published on Monday showed that of 39 primary dealers surveyed, 21 expect the Fed to hold rates steady, while 18 forecast a quarter point rise in the federal funds rate to 5.75 percent.
Some dealers said they will be keeping a close eye on possible comments by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, who is expected to speak at the Japan Society in New York at around 2330 GMT.
